body:
Martin @mkouba has helped to identify a possible issue with [SecurityidentityAssociation](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/security/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/security/runtime/SecurityIdentityAssociation.java).

The way it shows itself, as exposed by the [disabled test](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/6610), is that `SecurityIdentity` created by [OidcIdentityProvider.authenticate](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcIdentityProvider.java#L74) which creates a principal with a custom principal claim is missed when [OidcJsonWebTokenProducer](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcJsonWebTokenProducer.java) uses an injected `Securityidentity` to figure out which principal to return, and in the case of the failing test it looks like it picks up [this SecurityIdentity](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/security/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/security/runtime/SecurityIdentityAssociation.java#L46) and therefore a principal with a custom principal claim is missed
Is there an example of a failure somewhere? If the wrong bean was being provided by SecurityidentityAssociation then other tests would fail as well.

Actually I know what the problem is, or at least nearly sure :-).
So `JsonWebToken` is a `Principal` so we have 2 `Principal` producers, in [SecurityIdentityAssociation](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/security/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/security/runtime/SecurityIdentityAssociation.java#L25) and in [OidcIdentityProvider](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcJsonWebTokenProducer.java#L38).

I think the one in [SecurityIdentityAssociation](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/security/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/security/runtime/SecurityIdentityAssociation.java#L25) should be preferred when it comes to injecting a `Principal` because the producer there is a closer match.
Hi Martin, @mkouba, what do you think ?

@sberyozkin so the producer method declared on [OidcJsonWebTokenProducer](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcJsonWebTokenProducer.java#L37) should take precedence because it's declared on an enabled alternative bean (see https://docs.jboss.org/cdi/spec/2.0/cdi-spec.html#unsatisfied_and_ambig_dependencies for more information). Otherwise the build would fail with `AmbiguousResolutionException`. 

How and where do we set the `Principal` of the injected `SecurityIdentity`?

Hi @mkouba, thanks, the principal [is set here](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcIdentityProvider.java#L74).
But what happens is that by the time [this producer method](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcJsonWebTokenProducer.java#L38) is called, [this code](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcIdentityProvider.java#L74) has not run yet (and it is only exposed in CI :-))
[SecurityidentityAssociation](SecurityidentityAssociation) has [QuarkusIdentityProviderManagerImpl](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/security/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/security/runtime/QuarkusIdentityProviderManagerImpl.java#L81) injected which calls [OidcIdentityprovider](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcIdentityProvider.java#L74) and this [OidcIdentityprovider](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/oidc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/oidc/runtime/OidcIdentityProvider.java#L74)
 call apparently happens after `JsonWebToken` (-> `Principal`) has been produced

@stuartwdouglas I wonder if a non-blocking CompletableFuture `authenticate` call might cause it, it is hard to come up with any other explanation as to why I can't reproduce it locally (Georgios tried it to) but it fails in the CI
